attribute_fields.COMMENTS: Determine if corporation must file Texas franchise tax return. Checks for physical presence, economic nexus, or Texas registration.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in Texas (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets Texas economic nexus threshold ($500K Texas receipts)

rule.policy:
Texas franchise tax: No tax due (total revenue below $1.23M threshold).
Filing may still be required if: - Organized in Texas (Texas entity) - Registered to do business in Texas - Owes tax in another report year
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.002(d)(2) - No Tax Due Threshold Reference: Texas Comptroller Rule 3.586 - Filing Requirements Reference: Form 05-163 (No Tax Due Information Report)

Texas franchise tax filing required due to physical presence.
Physical presence includes: - Office or place of business in Texas - Employees working in Texas - Tangible property in Texas - Texas entity (organized under Texas law) - Registered to do business in Texas
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.001 - Definitions Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.0001 - Nexus Standards Reference: Form 05-158 (Texas Franchise Tax Report)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established - franchise tax calculation required result.tx_qualifies_for_no_tax_due = false;

rule.policy:
Texas franchise tax filing required due to economic nexus.
Economic nexus threshold: $500,000 in Texas receipts (sourced to Texas)
This is NOT the federal Wayfair standard ($100K). Texas has its own economic nexus threshold specific to franchise tax.
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.0001(a)(1) - Economic Nexus Reference: Texas Comptroller Rule 3.586(b) - Nexus Standards

No Texas nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not have: - Physical presence in Texas - $500,000 or more in Texas receipts
Any estimated franchise tax payments would be refunded.
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.0001 - Nexus Standards

attribute_fields.COMMENTS: Determine which deduction method produces the lowest franchise tax liability. Taxpayer can choose COGS, compensation, or 70% of revenue.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Has nexus and above no-tax-due threshold

condition.name: seventy_percent_greater
condition.comment: 70% of revenue is greater than both COGS and compensation

rule.policy: No franchise tax due - deduction method not applicable.

Texas franchise tax: Using 70% of revenue deduction method.
This simplified method allows businesses to deduct 70% of total revenue without tracking COGS or compensation. Often beneficial for: - Service businesses with low COGS - Businesses with high margins - Businesses wanting simplified calculation
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.1012(f) - Compensation Deduction Reference: Texas Comptroller Publication 96-1045, Section 3.6

Texas franchise tax: Using Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) deduction method.
COGS deduction includes: - Direct material costs - Direct labor costs - Manufacturing overhead - Inventory adjustments
COGS typically most beneficial for: - Manufacturing businesses - Retailers - Wholesalers - Businesses with significant inventory
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.1012(i) - COGS Deduction Reference: Texas Comptroller Rule 3.591 - COGS Calculation

Texas franchise tax: Using compensation deduction method.
Compensation includes: - Wages and cash compensation - Employee benefits (health insurance, retirement, etc.) - Payroll taxes paid by employer - Stock-based compensation
Compensation typically most beneficial for: - Service businesses - Professional services (law, accounting, consulting) - Technology companies - Businesses with high labor costs and low COGS
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.1012(f) - Compensation Deduction Reference: Texas Comptroller Rule 3.590 - Compensation Calculation

attribute_fields.COMMENTS: Calculate Texas taxable margin for franchise tax. Margin = Revenue - (COGS or Compensation or 70% of Revenue)

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Has nexus and above no-tax-due threshold

condition.name: qualifies_for_ez
condition.comment: Qualifies for E-Z computation ($20M or less in revenue)

rule.policy: No franchise tax due - margin calculation not applicable.

Texas franchise tax: Calculating taxable margin (standard method).
E-Z Computation option available: Business has $20M or less in revenue and may elect simplified E-Z computation instead of standard calculation.
E-Z Computation formula: - Tax = (Total Revenue - $1.23M) × 0.575% × TX Apportionment Factor - Much simpler than standard margin calculation - Often results in similar or lower tax
Standard Margin Calculation: 1. Total Revenue: [Revenue from all sources] 2. Deduction: - [COGS, Compensation, or 70% of revenue] 3. Taxable Margin: = [Result] 4. Texas Apportionment Factor: × [TX Receipts / Total Receipts] 5. Apportioned Margin: = [Final taxable margin]
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.1016 - E-Z Computation Reference: Texas Comptroller Form 05-169 (E-Z Computation) Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.101 - Tax Base

Texas franchise tax: Calculating taxable margin (standard method).
Standard Margin Calculation: 1. Total Revenue: [All revenue from business activities] 2. Deduction: - [COGS, Compensation, or 70% - taxpayer's choice] 3. Taxable Margin: = [Gross margin] 4. Texas Apportionment: × [TX Receipts / Total Receipts] 5. Apportioned Margin: = [Amount subject to franchise tax]
Texas uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% receipts). Receipts are sourced to Texas based on: - Sale of tangible property: Destination (where delivered) - Services: Where service is performed or received - Rentals: Location of property
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.101 - Tax Base (Taxable Margin) Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.106 - Apportionment Reference: Texas Comptroller Rule 3.591 - Apportionment

attribute_fields.COMMENTS: Calculate Texas franchise tax liability. Applies 0.75% or 0.375% rate to apportioned margin.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Has nexus and above no-tax-due threshold

condition.name: is_retail_wholesale
condition.comment: Primarily engaged in retail or wholesale trade

condition.name: use_ez_computation
condition.comment: Elects to use E-Z computation method

rule.policy:
No Texas franchise tax due.
Reasons: - No nexus with Texas, OR - Total revenue below $1.23M no-tax-due threshold
Any estimated franchise tax payments will be refunded.
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.002(d)(2) - No Tax Due Threshold

Texas franchise tax: E-Z Computation (simplified method).
E-Z Computation is available for businesses with $20M or less in revenue. This optional calculation is often simpler and may result in lower tax.
E-Z Computation Formula: 1. Total Revenue: [All revenue] 2. No Tax Due Threshold: - $1,230,000 3. Taxable Revenue: = [Result] 4. E-Z Computation Rate: × 0.575% (0.00575) 5. Texas Apportionment: × [TX Receipts / Total Receipts] 6. Franchise Tax Before Credits: = [Tax] 7. Credits: - [Film, R&D, enterprise zone, etc.] 8. Final Franchise Tax: = [Tax liability]
IMPORTANT: This is NOT an income tax. It is a privilege tax for doing business in Texas, calculated on gross margin rather than net income.
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.1016 - E-Z Computation Reference: Texas Comptroller Form 05-169 (E-Z Computation) Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.002 - Rate

Texas franchise tax: Standard margin calculation with retail/wholesale rate.
Reduced Rate Calculation (0.375%): 1. Total Revenue: [All revenue] 2. Deduction: - [COGS, Compensation, or 70% of revenue] 3. Taxable Margin: = [Gross margin] 4. Texas Apportionment: × [TX Receipts / Total Receipts] 5. Apportioned Margin: = [Margin subject to tax] 6. Retail/Wholesale Rate: × 0.375% (0.00375) 7. Franchise Tax Before Credits: = [Tax] 8. Credits: - [Available credits] 9. Final Franchise Tax: = [Tax liability]
Retail/Wholesale Reduced Rate: Businesses primarily engaged in retail or wholesale trade qualify for reduced 0.375% rate (half the standard rate).
"Primarily engaged" means more than 50% of gross receipts from retail/wholesale.
IMPORTANT: This is NOT an income tax. Texas has no corporate income tax. The franchise tax is a privilege tax for doing business in Texas.
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.002(b) - Retail/Wholesale Rate Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.0002(c) - "Primarily Engaged" Definition Reference: Texas Comptroller Publication 96-1045, Section 2.3

Texas franchise tax: Standard margin calculation with standard rate.
Standard Rate Calculation (0.75%): 1. Total Revenue: [All revenue from business] 2. Deduction: - [COGS, Compensation, or 70% - taxpayer choice] 3. Taxable Margin: = [Gross margin] 4. Texas Apportionment: × [TX Receipts / Total Receipts] 5. Apportioned Margin: = [Margin subject to franchise tax] 6. Standard Rate: × 0.75% (0.0075) 7. Franchise Tax Before Credits: = [Tax amount] 8. Credits: - [Film, R&D, enterprise zone, disabled veteran, etc.] 9. Final Franchise Tax: = [Tax liability]
IMPORTANT: This is NOT a corporate income tax. Texas has NO corporate income tax. The franchise tax is a privilege tax for the right to do business in Texas, based on gross margin rather than net income.
Key Differences from Income Tax: - Based on revenue and margin, not net income - No deduction for operating expenses (except via COGS/compensation) - Much lower rate (0.75% vs typical 5-10% income tax rates) - Different calculation methods available (COGS, compensation, 70%)
Available Credits: - Film, television, video game production - Enterprise zone project - Research and development activities - Disabled veteran business enterprise - Historic structure rehabilitation
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.002(a) - Standard Rate Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.101 - Tax Base (Margin) Reference: Texas Comptroller Form 05-158 (Franchise Tax Report) Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.001 - This is a franchise tax, not income tax

No Texas franchise tax due - zero or negative margin.
Possible reasons: - Deduction (COGS or compensation) equals or exceeds revenue - No receipts apportioned to Texas - Business operated at a loss
Any estimated franchise tax payments will be refunded.
Note: Unlike income tax, there is no loss carryforward for franchise tax. Each year stands alone.
Reference: TX Tax Code § 171.101 - Taxable Margin
